messages.text: Trying to verify the Nexus S1's that I received are S1.2.
I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Let me check what we have on the S1 revisions.
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · Nexus S1.2 miner hardware revision identify
Read github.com/BitLuckFW/ESP-Miner-Nexus
Searched the web · "Nexus S1.2" BitLuck miner board model
Read github.com/BitLuckFW/ESP-Miner-Nexus/releases/tag/v1.0.4.4
Searched the web · Nexus S1 miner "S1.2" version web UI device model
Handed to the team · No S1 vs S1.2 revision identification details in our product facts or the public

I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Happy to help you pin down the revision.

Two things I need, and I would rather confirm than guess:

1. A screenshot of the miner's web UI landing page (the one showing model, ASIC and firmware version). Open the miner's IP in a browser on the same network.
2. A photo of the label on the underside of one unit, the one with the serial on it.

I do not want to quote you a board marking from memory, so I have also pinged JD, our hardware lead, who knows exactly which mark separates the S1.2 from the first board. He or one of the team will come into this chat, and you will get it by email too if you step away.

If you want the fastest answer, JD is very active on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate with the same photos.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks, that is exactly the right shot. Here is what it shows:

1. Bottom left of the PCB silkscreen, under the Nexus Miner logo: **Model: S1, Ver: 2.1**. That is the board revision marking, so this unit is a Ver 2.1 board.
2. Screen reads BM1373, 10742 GH/s, 125.250 W, Vi 11875 mV, Vc 925 mV, 10546 mA, 55 C, fan 1293 RPM, uptime 19d 13h. That is a healthy S1: about 10.7 TH/s at 125 W is right on target, and 55 C with the fan barely at 1300 RPM is cool.

The one thing I will not guess at is whether "Ver: 2.1" is what the batch was sold as "S1.2", since that is a naming question on our side, not a reading of the board. JD has the revision list and is already pinged on this chat, so he can confirm the mapping.

Two things that would let him answer for the whole set:
1. Check the same silkscreen line on each of the other units and tell me if any read a different Ver number.
2. On the miner's web UI, the firmware version (top or in Settings).

Faster route if you want it now: Discord https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate with this same photo.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Clear as day now: the silkscreen reads **Model: S1, Ver.: 2.1**, right under the Nexus Miner logo. Also visible: the 15 A blade fuse, the +12V XT30 input and four R22 inductors, one per BM1373.

So the board itself calls this hardware revision 2.1. Whether our listing's "S1.2" refers to that same revision is a naming call, and JD has the revision list for it. He is already pinged on this chat and the team is in until 6pm Eastern.

While you wait, one thing that would settle the whole batch: check the same two lines on each of your other units and tell me if any read a Ver other than 2.1. If they all match, they are all the same board.
They all match

Good, that is the useful answer: every unit you received is the same board, Model S1 Ver. 2.1, so there is no mixed batch in what you got.

That is as far as I can take it from the hardware side. The last piece, whether Ver. 2.1 is the revision sold as S1.2, is JD's list and he already has this chat with your photos. The team is on until 6pm Eastern, and you will get the confirmation by email if you step away.

One more data point from your first photo, in case it matters to you: that unit is running 10.74 TH/s at 125 W, 55 C, 19 days uptime. That is exactly where a healthy four-chip BM1373 S1 should sit.

If you want JD directly, he is @nullhashrate on our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf
I'm asking because Harlolabs has OS for an S1.1
That changes the question into "which Harlo OS build do I flash", which is the right thing to get exactly right. Let me read the Harlo downloads page now.
Read harlolabs.com
Searched the web · Harlo OS harlolabs downloads Nexus S1.1 firmware
Read heliumdeploy.com/pages/harlo-os
Read harlolabs.com

That is the detail that matters, and it changes my advice: do not flash anything until this is confirmed.

Here is the likely explanation, and why I will not treat it as settled:

1. We sell two separate products, the **NEXUS S1** (four BM1373, about 10 TH/s) and the **NEXUS S1-1** (a single BM1373, about 5 TH/s). A Harlo profile written "S1.1" is most likely the single chip S1-1 model, not revision 1 of your board.
2. Your boards are the four chip S1, silkscreened Model S1, Ver. 2.1. Flashing a single chip profile onto a four chip board is exactly the kind of mismatch that gives you a quarter of your hashrate or a unit that will not come up.

So: leave them on the stock Nexus firmware for now. They are running well, 10.74 TH/s at 125 W.

I cannot open the Harlo flasher list from here, so I am not going to tell you which profile is right from guesswork. JD builds Harlo OS and I have given him your board photos and this question.
Handed to the team · Cannot open the harlolabs.com flasher profile list from here; need JD to confirm

He or the team will come back in this chat, and you get it by email if you step away. Fastest path if you want it in the next few minutes: Discord https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate and post the Ver. 2.1 silkscreen photo with the question "which profile for a four chip S1".
But i'm guessing these are S1.2

Fair guess, and it might be right. Both readings are live:

1. "S1.1" means the single chip S1-1 model.
2. "S1.1" means S1 revision 1, which would make your Ver. 2.1 boards the ones people call S1.2.

Your silkscreen says Ver. 2.1, which honestly leans toward your reading. But leaning is not enough to pick a flash image, and a wrong profile on a four chip board is the one mistake that costs you a working miner.

One thing that would strengthen your case while JD gets back to you: the stock Nexus firmware carries its own model string. In the Nexus web UI (http://192.168.4.22 from your screen), open the system or settings page and tell me the exact model and firmware version it prints. Their recent builds use names like S1_4 for the four chip board, so that string plus the Ver. 2.1 silkscreen is what pins it down.
nexus.v1.0.4.4

That is the firmware build, and good news there: 
v1.0.4.4 is the newest public Nexus firmware release, the one that added multi-pool support and the new Nexus S1_4 Pro hardware model
, published Sep 4. So your units are current, nothing to update on the stock side.

What I still need is the separate hardware/model field, not the version string. On the Nexus web UI it usually sits on the same system page, a line reading something like "Model" or "Board" with a value such as S1_4 or S1_4 Pro. If you see it, tell me the exact text.

If that line does not exist in your UI, say so and we stop there: JD has your Ver. 2.1 photos and the S1.1 profile question already, and he can answer it outright. He is @nullhashrate on https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf if you want it faster than email.
NexusS1 (BM1373)

That closes out everything the hardware itself can tell us. The firmware reports a plain **NexusS1 (BM1373)** with no revision suffix, so the stock software does not encode the board rev at all. The only revision marking on these units is the silkscreen: **Model S1, Ver. 2.1**, identical across every unit you received.

So the full picture for JD, and for you if you post it in Discord:

1. Board silkscreen: Model S1, Ver. 2.1, same on all units.
2. Firmware model string: NexusS1 (BM1373), no suffix.
3. Firmware version: nexus.v1.0.4.4, the current public release.
4. Four BM1373, four R22 inductors, 15 A blade fuse, XT30 12 V input, running 10.74 TH/s at 125 W, 55 C.

Whether that Ver. 2.1 board is what the Harlo flasher calls S1.1 or what people call S1.2 is a naming question only JD can answer, and I would rather he said it than that I guessed. He has all of the above.

Until he does: do not flash. Your units are current and running on target, so there is nothing you lose by waiting.

Faster route: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate.
ok, thank you

You are welcome. JD has the board photos and the profile question, and the team is on until 6pm Eastern, so you should hear back shortly either here or by email.

Nice fleet, by the way. 125 W for 10.7 TH/s with the fan at 1300 RPM is about as good as that board gets.
